description:
About the Position

TU Delft invites applications for a PhD position in foil drone research. The project develops unmanned vehicles that operate both in air and water using hydrofoil dynamics, studying how such dual-domain drones can transition between flying and foil-borne operation efficiently and autonomously.

The doctoral candidate will work on the aerodynamics and hydrodynamics of foil-based flight, prototype vehicle designs, and develop the control and autonomy stack needed for real transitions between air and water operation. The work combines flight testing, tank or open-water experiments and simulation, and the position is embedded in the university's leading drone research environment.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, robotics or a related field, with strong analytical and hands-on prototyping skills. Experience with flight control, system identification or fluid dynamics is an advantage. The appointment follows the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement with the national PhD salary scale and a four-year contract structure.

Highlights

  • Hydrofoil dynamics for air-water drones
  • Vehicle prototyping and flight testing
  • Control and autonomy for domain transitions
  • Aerodynamic and hydrodynamic modelling
  • Dual-domain unmanned vehicle design
  • Salaried PhD, EUR 3,204 - 4,051 per month (CAO-NU scale)
